text:
matt: quick thread — we ran the kernel-selector rollout on staging and the continuous-batching heuristics need per-GPU ceiling tuning. summary below.

jia: please paste the raw numbers when you have them, want to eyeball.

matt: short version: throughput up on A100/H100 but A10/T4 regressed to OOMs or huge p95. L4 is in-between. observed issue seems to be token-budget + kernel choice combos that push working set over memory on the smaller amps.

kevin: got an example config that caused the OOM? :eyes:

matt: yes, reproduced with the new selector preferring fused-attn int8 kernel for short sequences. snippet from the test harness:

```
# per-device ceilings used in the canary
max_batch_size: 64
max_tokens_per_batch: 24576
queue_timeout_ms: 50
token_budget_target_per_gpu: 120000
per_gpu_overcommit: false
```

sara: that's pretty aggressive for A10/T4. their model KV + activation memory kills on batch_size 64 for long-seq workloads.

matt: exactly. here's the 15-min perf summary (staging, dist-ml-run-42):
- H100: throughput +18%, p50 22ms -> 20ms, p95 +2ms
- A100: throughput +11%, p50 27ms -> 25ms, p95 +3ms
- L4: throughput +6%, p50 33ms -> 31ms, p95 +10ms
- A10: throughput -4% (higher retries), p95 +120ms, occasional OOMs
- T4: throughput -12%, frequent small OOM spikes at seq_len>1024

jia: interesting that p95 increased on L4 despite small gain in throughput — likely queuing amplification from larger batches.

matt: diagnosis: kernel-selector picks faster int8 kernels which reduce compute time but increase transient memory due to fused buffers + larger KV prefetch. With continuous batching, batch formation tries to reach max_tokens_per_batch which amplifies memory usage.

kevin: proposal time. we should set per-GPU ceilings that cap both batch count and tokens-per-batch. something like:

```
# proposal (per-gpu)
H100: max_batch_size=128, max_tokens_per_batch=262144
A100: max_batch_size=96,  max_tokens_per_batch=196608
L4:  max_batch_size=48,  max_tokens_per_batch=65536
A10: max_batch_size=32,  max_tokens_per_batch=49152
T4:  max_batch_size=24,  max_tokens_per_batch=40960
```

sara: those look reasonable as starting points. For A10/T4 we should also reduce `queue_timeout_ms` to 20ms so smaller batches form faster and reduce memory tail.

matt: agree. also we need a small change in kernel-selector heuristics: prefer memory-slim kernel variants when estimated transient memory > threshold (e.g., 60% of GPU free). fallback to fused kernel only if below.

jia: how do we estimate transient memory? we already have a fast estimator in runtime-profiler — just need to expose it to selector.

matt: yes, plan:
1) implement per-GPU ceiling matrix in batching config
2) add memory-aware preference flag in kernel-selector
3) lower queue_timeout_ms for smaller devices
4) run 30min canary across regional clusters (us-west/us-east-eu) with perf-bot collecting p50/p95/ooms

kevin: can we also add an adaptive token_budget_target that decays when OOMs detected? e.g., minus 10% for next minute.

matt: good idea — simpler than rolling back entire selector. add `oom_backoff_pct` default 10% and cooldown 60s.

perf-bot: scheduled canary: rollout window 12:30-13:30 UTC, groups: h100-canary(20%), a100(20%), l4(15%), a10(15%), t4(15%). collectors: perf-telemetry, kv-evictions, runtime-logs.

oncall-bot: alert rule created: "batching-memory-exceeded" -> page if OOM rate > 0.5% for 5min.

sara: who owns the rollout PR? I can pick up the batching-config and queue_timeout change.

kevin: I can handle kernel-selector tweak and the oom_backoff logic.

jia: I'll wire perf-bot dashboards and add the per-device metrics to the console.

matt: excellent. next steps: PRs today, canary tomorrow morning. I'll drop the exact config into the repo: `infra/runtime/batching/ceilings.yaml` and link here once created. cc @kevin @sara :thumbsup:

kevin: :thumbsup:

sara: :rocket:

matt: last note — keep quantization profiles pinned per-model for canary. one regression we saw earlier was a model getting auto-swapped to q4_0 which increased transient cache size. lock profiles for canary.

jia: noted, will pin model profiles in canary configs.

matt: thanks all — will post PR links and the canonical numbers after the 30-min run.
